This integration connects Gladys Assistant to a **Google Wifi**, **Nest Wifi** (router) or
**OnHub** (TP-Link or ASUS) Wi-Fi system. It tells Gladys whether the internet is up, which
devices are on the Wi-Fi, how fast the connection is, and lets a scene pause a device's internet
or restart the Wi-Fi.

Requires **Gladys 5.3 or later**.

## Two ways to reach the Wi-Fi

| Channel          | What you need                                | What you get                                                                                                  |
| ---------------- | -------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| **Local**        | The IP address of the router                 | Internet state, WAN cable, uptime, firmware, available update, public address                                 |
| **Google cloud** | A Google refresh token (see below), optional | Connected devices (presence), live throughput, speed test, number of devices, Wi-Fi points, pause and restart |

Both can be used together; most people start with the local channel only, it needs no account.

The Configuration screen shows the standard **Prefer the local connection** switch. When it is on
(default), the internet state comes from the router itself; off, it comes from the Google cloud.
Each device shows a badge with the channel it really uses: _local_, _cloud_, or _unreachable_.
When the router does not answer on the LAN but the cloud does, the router badge turns to _cloud_
with an orange dot.

## Set up the local channel

1. Find the address of the **main** Wi-Fi point (the one plugged into your internet box). On a
   Google Wifi network left at its factory settings, it is `192.168.86.1`. In the Google Home app:
   **Wi-Fi → Settings → Advanced networking → LAN**.
2. Enter it in **Router address (local)** and save.
3. Click **Test the connection**: the answer shows the model, the firmware and the internet state.

The integration reads `http://<address>/api/v1/status`, the status page the router serves on the
local network without any password. It only reads: nothing can be changed through it.

Gladys must be able to reach that address: when Gladys is on another subnet, allow it in your
firewall.

## Set up the Google cloud channel (optional)

The cloud channel uses the API of the Google Home app. **Google does not document it**: it works
today, it may change one day. It needs a **refresh token** of the Google account that manages the
Wi-Fi.

1. Get a refresh token for the Google Wifi app. Community tools do the Google sign-in for you and
   show the token, which starts with `1//`. Search for "Google Wifi refresh token" or "OnHub auth
   tool": use one you trust, it sees your Google sign-in.
2. Paste the token in **Google refresh token** and save.
3. Click **Test the connection**: the answer lists the Wi-Fi systems and the number of connected
   devices.

The token is stored in Gladys in a secret field, never shown back, never written to the logs and
only sent to Google. To revoke it, remove the Google Wifi / Google Home access in your Google
account security settings (Third-party connections), then paste a new one.

## Devices

Open **Discovery** in the integration page and add the devices you want.

| Device                                       | Channel | Features                                                                                                           |
| -------------------------------------------- | ------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| **Google Wifi router**                       | local   | Internet (on/off), WAN cable connected, uptime (days), update available, firmware (text), public address (text)    |
| **Wi-Fi _name_** (the network)               | cloud   | Internet, live download and upload (Mb/s), last speed test download and upload (Mb/s), number of connected devices |
| **Wi-Fi point _room_**                       | cloud   | Online, light ring brightness (0-100 %, can be changed)                                                            |
| **Connected devices** (phone, computer, TV…) | cloud   | Connected (presence), internet access (switch: off pauses its internet), live download and upload                  |

Google remembers every device that ever joined the Wi-Fi: Discovery only lists the ones connected
right now, plus the ones you already added. Turn off **Show the connected devices in Discovery** to
hide them.

The values are refreshed every **Refresh interval** (60 s by default). Only the values that change
are sent to Gladys.

## Scenes

### Triggers

| Trigger                 | When                                             | Variables                        |
| ----------------------- | ------------------------------------------------ | -------------------------------- |
| Internet lost           | The router reports the internet is down          | `source` (local / cloud)         |
| Internet restored       | The internet is back                             | `source`, `offline_minutes`      |
| Device joined the Wi-Fi | A device connects (filter: one device, or any)   | `name`, `ip`                     |
| Device left the Wi-Fi   | A device disconnects (filter: one device or any) | `name`, `ip`                     |
| Wi-Fi point offline     | A point stops answering                          | `name`                           |
| Router update available | The router announces a new firmware              | `current_version`, `new_version` |

Each trigger fires once per change, never again while nothing changes. A router that simply stops
answering is not taken for an internet outage.

### Actions

| Action                    | What it does                                           | Outputs                                 |
| ------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------ | --------------------------------------- |
| Pause a device's internet | Pauses (or resumes) the internet of one device (cloud) | `paused`                                |
| Run a speed test          | Measures the internet speed, about a minute (cloud)    | `download_mbps`, `upload_mbps`          |
| Restart the Wi-Fi         | Restarts one point, or every point (cloud)             | `restarted`                             |
| Check the internet        | Reads the router now                                   | `online`, `source`, `connected_clients` |

Example: "every school day at 21:00, pause the internet of the children's tablet; at 7:00, resume
it".

## Dashboard widgets

- **Wi-Fi status**: internet, firmware, update, uptime, connected devices, Wi-Fi points, last
  speed test, live throughput (once the network device is added) and a **Run a speed test** button.
- **Wi-Fi devices**: the devices on the Wi-Fi right now, busiest first, with a badge when one is
  paused or on the guest network.

## Configuration screen buttons

- **Test the connection**: reads both channels now and says what answered.
- **Run a speed test** (cloud).
- **Restart the Wi-Fi** (cloud): tick the confirmation box first. Every point restarts: no network
  for a few minutes, Gladys included if it uses the Wi-Fi.

## Troubleshooting

- **"Router unreachable on the local network"**: check the address, and that Gladys can reach it
  (`curl http://192.168.86.1/api/v1/status` from the Gladys machine). Use the main point, not an
  extension.
- **"Google refused the refresh token"**: the token was revoked or mistyped: generate a new one.
- **Throughput or speed test stay empty**: some systems do not report them; the rest still works.
- **A device has a strange name**: rename it in the Google Home app, or in Gladys.

## Privacy

The local channel never leaves your network. The cloud channel only talks to Google, with your own
token. The integration stores nothing outside the Gladys configuration.

## Configuration settings

These are the settings Google Wifi / OnHub asks for in its configuration screen in Gladys.

| Setting | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Getting started | `section` | No | Two ways to reach your Wi-Fi, usable together. Local: the router's own status page on your network, no account needed (internet state, firmware, uptime). Google cloud: with a Google refresh token, the connected devices, live throughput, speed test, internet pause and restart. |
| Router address (local) | `string` | No | IP address of the main Wi-Fi point, the one plugged into your box. 192.168.86.1 on a Google Wifi network left at its factory settings. Leave empty to disable the local channel. |
| Google cloud (optional) | `section` | No | The cloud channel uses the unofficial Google API of the Google Home app. It needs a refresh token of the Google account that manages the Wi-Fi: the documentation explains how to get one. The token stays in Gladys and is only sent to Google. |
| Google refresh token | `secret` | No | Leave empty to use the local channel only. |
| Show the connected devices in Discovery | `boolean` | No | Cloud only. Each phone, computer or TV on the Wi-Fi can then be added to Gladys: presence, throughput and internet pause. |
| Refresh interval (s) | `number` | No | How often the router is read, in seconds (30 to 3600). |

## How to install Google Wifi / OnHub in Gladys

1. In Gladys, open **Integrations**: Google Wifi / OnHub appears in the catalog, next to the native integrations, with a community badge.
2. Click **Install**. Gladys pulls the Docker image (`ghcr.io/prohand/gladys-googlewifionhub:1.0.1`), starts it in a sandbox isolated from the core, and generates the integration's interface (devices, discovery and configuration).
3. Open the **Configuration** screen of the integration, fill in the settings, and save.
4. You can also install it directly from its repository URL: [https://github.com/prohand/gladys-googlewifionhub](https://github.com/prohand/gladys-googlewifionhub).

Google Wifi / OnHub requires Gladys `>=5.3.0`. The catalog inside Gladys refreshes every hour, so a new version becomes available at most one hour after its release.

Not running Gladys yet? It is free and open source: [follow the installation guide](/docs/) to get started.

## About external integrations

Google Wifi / OnHub is an **external integration**: a community integration packaged as a Docker container and published on GitHub, that Gladys installs in one click and runs in a sandbox isolated from its core. It is published and maintained by [prohand](https://github.com/prohand), not by the Gladys core team.
